title: Autonomous Structural Discovery Of Bioprocess Dynamics And Kinetics Via LLM-Driven Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.35391v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: High-fidelity digital twins in continuous biomanufacturing are often bottlenecked by incomplete kinetic models, while standard data-driven algorithms (e.g., SINDy, PINNs) lack interpretability or impose rigid physical assumptions. This paper introduces a hybrid closed-loop architecture for autonomous kinetic state-space discovery driven by a Large Language Model (LLM) agent. The framework employs a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology across orthogonal operational regimes. This algorithmic peeling mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (catalytic) biological rate law. Grounded in a Two-Level Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) library, the framework utilizes Moving Horizon Estimation (MHE) and logarithmic decomposition to decouple complex cell growth kinetics into orthogonal multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) residual channels. tldr: 该论文提出了一种由大语言模型智能体驱动的混合闭环架构，通过“隔离-剥离”方法论和对数分解，自主发现并数学解耦生物制造过程中相互纠缠的乘性（抑制性）与加性（调节性）动力学机制。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces an LLM-agent-driven hybrid closed-loop architecture that autonomously discovers and mathematically decouples entangled multiplicative (inhibitory) and additive (regulatory) kinetic mechanisms in bioprocesses through a sequential "isolation-peeling" methodology and logarithmic decomposition.
